title: Flourishing Skin Europe: A multicenter European cross-sectional study on values and humor in psoriasis and atopic dermatitis
summary: People with psoriasis or atopic dermatitis often experience not only physical symptoms but also emotional and social burdens in everyday life. Previous research has mainly focused on problems and impairment, while much less is known about personal strengths and attitudes that may be linked to better well-being. This Europe-wide study therefore examines how personal values and the way people use humor are related to psychological and social well-being in adults with these skin diseases. Participants are recruited at dermatology centers in different European countries during routine clinical visits. After giving written informed consent, they complete a one-time anonymous questionnaire on site; in addition, study staff document selected clinical background information from routine care. The study aims to improve understanding of health-promoting personal resources among people with chronic inflammatory skin diseases across Europe.

interventions.name: Adult patients with psoriasis or atopic dermatitis are approached at participating dermatology centers during routine clinical visits. After receiving study information and providing written informed consent, eligibility is checked by the study staff. Data are then collected once in an anonymous man

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosed psoriasis or atopic dermatitis; residence in one of the participating European countries; written informed consent for voluntary study participation; sufficient language skills to independently understand and complete the questionnaire version in the respective local language.
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient language skills preventing independent understanding or completion of the questionnaire; severe psychotic or other acute psychiatric disorders that preclude reliable participation or informed consent; presence of another chronic inflammatory skin disease other than psoriasis or atopic dermatitis.
